symptom: After materializing more than one storyboard design, one-click or Agent-assisted arranging could interleave shots from different designs on the canonical timeline because equal shot numbers were treated as one storyboard.
direct_cause: The canvas-to-timeline planner treated an omitted nodeIds list as every shot-numbered canvas node even though materialized nodes already carried distinct storyboardDesignId provenance.
class_root: Storyboard provenance was recorded at materialization but not enforced at the final selection boundary before timeline adoption, so a project-level canvas was incorrectly assumed to contain one storyboard.
affected_population: Users who materialize two or more storyboard designs in one project and then use the timeline one-click arrange action
Agent and Production Run callers that arrange canvas nodes without an exact node subset
internal_only_reason: The failure is an internal provenance-selection contract between Nomi canvas nodes and timeline adoption. No provider, model, MCP host, or external editing engine determines the correct storyboard scope.
invariants: A user-facing arrange operation with an active storyboard design selects only shot nodes whose storyboardDesignId exactly matches that design.
An Agent node subset spanning multiple non-empty storyboardDesignId values is rejected before any timeline mutation.
An unscoped legacy operation is allowed only when provenance resolves to zero or one distinct storyboard design; multiple designs fail closed as ambiguous.
A Production Run passes only its adopted generation job node ids to production.arrange.
migration: No persisted schema changes. Existing legacy canvases with no storyboardDesignId retain whole-canvas arranging. Canvases with exactly one provenance id infer that design. Canvases with multiple ids now require an active design or explicit node ids.
residual_risks: Legacy nodes without provenance cannot be assigned to a particular modern storyboard automatically; explicit node selection remains the safe compatibility path.
The canonical timeline still represents one adopted cut. Switching the selected storyboard does not replace or fork an existing timeline automatically.
